params.body:
## Why

The dropdowns on the vehicle sheet came out of the database in insertion order. "Lakwerk/verf" read Vast, Metaal, Parelmoer, Mat, Aangepast, Crystal effect, Metaal tweekleurig, Mica, Mica tweekleurig, Pica, so a dealer had to scan the whole list every single time instead of jumping to the letter.

The cause was never a missing feature: `DbRepository::pluck($param1, $param2, $order, $where, $languageCheck, $with_empty_pair)` has always accepted an order, and the calls that fill these lists passed `null`.

One catch made this more than passing `['name', 'asc']`. With `$languageCheck` on, the displayed column is `name_<lang>` (`name_nl`, `name_fr`, `name_en`, `name_de`); ordering on `name` would order on a column the user never sees, and on `vehicle_colors`, `vehicle_paint_types` and friends that column does not exist at all. So `pluck()` now resolves an order on the displayed column through the same language suffix. An explicitly named column (`['name_nl', 'asc']`) is left exactly as the caller wrote it, and a call without an order still gets no order, so nothing else in the app moves. No existing call combines an order on `name` with `$languageCheck = true`, so every current caller keeps its behaviour byte for byte.

## Inventory

Every `pluck()` that feeds a `<select>` on the vehicle sheet, in `app/Livewire/VehicleForm.php` (Livewire sheet) and `app/Http/Controllers/Vehicle/OwnStockController.php` (classic sheet, `create()`, `edit()` and `populateBodyStyles()`). The classic sheet's view composer (`OwnStockComposer`) fills no lists at all; it only sets `carpass_connected`.

| List | Current order | New order |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paint types (`vehicle_paint_types`) | none (`null`) → insertion order | `name` in the user's language, asc |
| Colours (`vehicle_colors`) | none (`null`) | `name` in the user's language, asc |
| Body styles (`vehicle_body_styles`) | `name_nl`, always Dutch | `name` in the user's language, asc |
| Fuel types (`vehicle_fuel_types`) | `name_nl`, always Dutch | `name` in the user's language, asc |
| Transmission types (`vehicle_transmission_types`) | none (`null`) | `name` in the user's language, asc |
| Usage categories (`vehicle_usage_categories`) | none (`null`) | `name` in the user's language, asc |
| Categories (`vehicle_categories`) | none (`null`) | `name` in the user's language, asc |
| Manufacturers (`manufacturers`) | `name` asc (via `Enumeration::getManufacturers()`) | unchanged, already alphabetical; the table has one untranslated `name` |
| Models (`models`) | `name` asc | unchanged, already alphabetical |
| Locations (`dealer_locations`) | `name` asc | unchanged, already alphabetical |
| Countries (`countries`) | `name` asc | unchanged, already alphabetical |
| Construction year | descending years (now → 1900) | unchanged: a natural order, and the recent years the dealer needs are on top |
| Doors, seats | not lists on this sheet (numeric inputs) | unchanged |
| Euronorm, VAT percentage, cleanliness/engine condition, availability in months, radius | hardcoded scales and enumerations | unchanged: a scale (very bad → perfect) and a numeric progression are their own order |
| Option values (`option_values`, the per-option dropdowns on the Opties tab) | insertion order, read from the relation in the blade, not via `pluck()` | unchanged: a per-option value set is often a scale ("1 zone / 2 zones / 3 zones"), so alphabetical would be a step backwards. Flagged here rather than changed |

**Curated order columns:** checked every one of these tables for a `sort_order` / `pdf_sort_order` (or comparable) column, in `database/schema/mysql-schema.sql` and in the migrations added since. **None of them carries one**, so there is no existing order to respect and nothing that would be overruled. Nothing was invented: where the data already carries an order (the scales above, the years) the list was left alone.

## What changed

- `app/Repositories/DbRepository.php`: `languageColumn()` and `languageOrder()` pulled out of `pluck()`. `languageOrder()` only rewrites the order when the caller ordered on the very column it displays; otherwise it returns the order untouched. `pluck()` itself is otherwise unchanged.
- `app/Repositories/OwnStock/{BodyStyle,Manufacturers,VehicleModel}Repository.php`: these three override `pluck()` with their own copy of the language line (a `whereNot`, a join, a stocklist join). They now use the same two helpers, so the rule lives in one place.
- `app/Livewire/VehicleForm.php` and `app/Http/Controllers/Vehicle/OwnStockController.php`: the seven lists above ask for `['name', 'asc']`. The two that hardcoded `name_nl` now follow the reader's language instead of always Dutch.
- `tests/Feature/VehicleSheetOptionOrderTest.php`: five tests. Every list seeded deliberately out of order, with a Dutch and an English label that disagree about what comes first, so an order on the wrong column cannot pass. One test for the Livewire sheet's view data, one for the classic sheet's repository calls, one proving the order follows the user's language, one proving an explicit column and a call without an order keep their old behaviour, and one proving the selected value still round-trips (it is still selected on mount, it is still offered by the reordered list, and it is still what the database holds after a save). Both halves were mutation-checked: putting `null` back in one call site, and defusing `languageOrder()`, each make the suite fail.

## Data findings (not fixed, a question for Ilse)

These hang off existing vehicles, so they are data decisions, not an edit to make in passing:

- **"Pica"** in the paint list looks like a typo for **"Mica"**, which is in the same list twice over ("Mica", "Mica tweekleurig"). If it is a typo, merging it into Mica means repointing the vehicles that carry it; renaming it alone would leave those vehicles on a value nobody chose on purpose.
- **"Aangepast"** reads like a catch-all rather than a paint type. Worth knowing whether it means "custom paintwork" (a real answer) or "none of the above" (a hole in the list), because the two want different fixes.

## Checked

- `APP_KEY=… php artisan view:cache` → Blade templates cached successfully.
- `php artisan test --filter='VehicleForm|OwnStock|Vehicle|SmokeTest|Pluck|Repository'` → 13 passed, 570 assertions, 0 failures.
- Full suite: 49 passed, 1893 assertions. The single failure is `BuildStampTest` (`/.well-known/build.json` → 404), which needs a build stamp this worktree has no deploy to produce; unrelated to this change.
- Local MySQL over `/tmp/mysql.sock`, database loaded from `database/schema/mysql-schema.sql` plus the post-2026-07-28 migrations, the way CI does it. No `.env` read or written.
params.title: Vehicle sheet: the dropdowns in a predictable order
